title: In vitro Synthesis of Native, Fibrous Long Spacing and Segmental Long Spacing Collagen
protocol: Combine 6 μl of water, 20 μl of 200 mM Na2HPO4 adjusted to pH 7 with HCl and 10 μl of 400 mM KCl in a microfuge tube and mix.
Add 4 μl of collagen monomer (~3 mg/ml in 0.01 N HCl) to the microfuge tube and mix.
Place the microfuge tube containing the reaction mixture in a heat block pre-warmed to 37 °C for 3 to 4 hr.
Dialyze 1 ml of collagen monomer (~3 mg/ml in 0.01 N HCl) using a 12-14 kDa MWCO membrane against 400 ml of water, changing the water four times over 24 hr at room temperature.
Combine 20 μl of water, 20 μl of 3 mg/ml α1-acid glycoprotein in water and 20 μl of dialyzed collagen monomer in a microfuge tube.
Leave the microfuge tube containing the reaction mixture at room temperature for 30 min.
Combine 67 μl of water, 60 μl of 100 mM glycine-HCl buffer at pH 3.3 and 40 μl of 10 mg/ml ATP in water in a microfuge tube and mix.
Add 33 μl of collagen monomer (~3 mg/ml in 0.01 N HCl) to the microfuge tube and mix.
Leave the microfuge tube containing the reaction mixture at room temperature for 2 hr.
Cleave the surface of a piece of mica attached to an AFM substrate by covering the mica surface with a piece of sticky tape and then peeling it away.
Check the tape afterwards to confirm that an entire layer of mica was cleaved.
Apply 20 μl of the collagen fibril solution to the freshly cleaved mica substrate.
Leave for 5 min.
Gently rinse off solution of collagen fibril with water, applying the water at the edge of the mica substrate and allowing it to flow across the sample.
Dry the surface under a gentle stream of nitrogen gas, directing the stream at the edge of the mica substrate.
Under an optical microscope at 200× magnification, observe native and FLS collagen samples for clumps of fibrils.
Observe SLS collagen under the same conditions; it should not be visible.
Image native collagen fibrils with an AFM in intermittent contact mode using silicon AFM probes.
Image FLS and SLS collagen fibrils with an AFM in contact mode using silicon nitride AFM probes.
Scan samples initially at 100 × 100 μm² to show several collagen constructs.
Zoom into a 10 × 10 μm² scan size for detailed observations of banding periodicity or finer features.
Further zoom into a 2 × 2 μm² scan size to observe banding periodicity in native and FLS collagen, or fine features in SLS collagen.
Check at least two other regions on the collagen sample to verify representativeness.
